chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Christians of the Arabs, 'Is their slaughter permissible to eat?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) forbade their slaughter, their hunted prey, and intermarrying with them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Arab Christians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the juristic distinction made by the Ahl al-Bayt between Arab Christians and other People of the Book, specifically regarding the permissibility of their meat and intermarriage. By citing the practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), it underscores a conservative stance that treats Arab Christians similarly to Jews in terms of dietary laws, reflecting the historical context of their distinct religious identity in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia.
